name: French Tech Rise
description: French Tech Rise is a Bpifrance grant program supporting early-stage French deep tech startups working on hardware, biotech, AI, or other industrial technologies. The grant covers up to 70% of eligible R&D and prototype costs, up to €500K. It targets pre-Series A companies with a genuinely innovative technical approach and a credible path to market. Applicants must be incorporated in France. The program prioritizes physical-world innovations — startups working on atoms, not just bits — distinguishing it from purely software-focused French programs.

name: Horizon Europe (Clusters)
description: Horizon Europe is the EU’s main research and innovation framework program (2021–2027) with a total budget of €95.5B. It is organized into thematic clusters: Health; Culture, Creativity & Society; Civil Security; Digital, Industry & Space; Climate, Energy & Mobility; and Food, Bioeconomy & Environment. Startups and SMEs apply to specific published calls within these clusters, typically as part of collaborative consortia (though some calls are open to individual entities). Each call has a defined scope, budget, and deadline. The EU Funding & Tenders portal is the single entry point for all applications.

name: Innosuisse Startup Grant
amount: Up to CHF 150K per phase (3 phases = up to CHF 450K total)
description: Innosuisse (Swiss Innovation Agency) offers Startup Grants to science-based Swiss startups with a clear link to a Swiss research institution. The program has three phases: Feasibility (up to CHF 150K, ~6 months), Proof of Concept (up to CHF 150K, ~12 months), and Market Entry (up to CHF 150K, ~12 months), for a potential total of CHF 450K. Each phase is applied for separately and must be completed successfully before advancing. Participation in Innosuisse coaching and training modules is mandatory alongside the grant. Startups must be in the process of spinning off from ETH, EPFL, a cantonal university, or a UAS.

name: ZIM Program (Central Innovation Programme for SMEs)
amount: Up to €380K per project (~45–55% of eligible costs)
description: ZIM (Zentrales Innovationsprogramm Mittelstand) is Germany’s largest and most accessible innovation funding program, administered by BMWK. It supports R&D projects by German SMEs (and startups) across all technology sectors and industries. Three funding forms: solo R&D projects (company alone), cooperative R&D projects (company + research institution), and R&D cooperation networks. The subsidy covers 45–55% of eligible R&D costs up to €380K per company per project. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, with evaluation taking roughly 3 months. There is no thematic restriction — any technologically novel project qualifies.

name: VLAIO Research Project Grant
amount: Up to €3M; 25–60% of eligible costs (higher for SMEs)
description: VLAIO (Flanders Innovation & Entrepreneurship) provides R&D project grants to companies based in the Flemish Region of Belgium. It funds both industrial research (further from market) and experimental development (closer to market), with subsidy rates of 25–50% for large companies, up to 60% for SMEs, and higher rates for collaborative projects. Maximum grant is €3M per project. The project must clearly exceed the state of the art and have commercial potential. Applications require a detailed technical and financial plan. VLAIO also offers innovation consulting, scale-up support, and connections to Flemish research institutions via its broader innovation ecosystem.

name: EIC Pathfinder
description: EIC Pathfinder funds visionary, high-risk research aimed at developing the scientific foundations for radically new future technologies. It has two tracks: Pathfinder Open (up to €3M for any scientific direction, consortia of at least 3 entities) and Pathfinder Challenges (up to €4M for specific thematic calls). Primarily targets research teams, universities, and science-based startups at TRL 1–4. Successful Pathfinder projects can feed directly into EIC Transition funding for further development toward market.

name: Innovation Norway
amount: Phase 1: up to NOK 150K; Phase 2: up to NOK 1M; Phase 3: up to NOK 2M
description: Innovation Norway offers startup grants to Norwegian companies under 3 years old with scalable, market-oriented innovations. The program has three sequential phases: Phase 1 (up to NOK 150K) for market and customer validation; Phase 2 (up to NOK 1M) for prototype development and business model refinement; Phase 3 (up to NOK 2M) for commercialization and internationalization. Each phase must be completed before applying for the next. Green tech and sustainability-focused startups receive priority weighting. Innovation Norway also provides international market access support, mentorship, and connections to its global network of offices.

name: EIC Step (European Innovation Council)
description: EIC Step is a European Innovation Council instrument under Horizon Europe that provides blended finance — combining a non-dilutive grant of up to €2.5M with an equity investment of up to €7.5M from the EIC Fund — to deep tech startups and SMEs developing breakthrough innovations with strong market potential. It targets companies that have already demonstrated technical feasibility and are ready to scale. The EIC Fund takes a minority equity stake in exchange for the investment component. Applications are submitted via the EIC platform and evaluated in a two-stage process including a written proposal and panel interview.

name: EIC Accelerator
amount: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €15M equity investment
description: The EIC Accelerator is the flagship EIC funding instrument for individual startups and SMEs with high-risk, high-impact innovations targeting large markets. It offers up to €2.5M in grants and up to €15M in equity investment (blended finance), or a grant-only option. Open to any tech sector, with strong focus on deep tech, green, and digital. Acceptance rates are typically 3–5%. Applications go through a three-stage process: short application, full proposal, and in-person panel interview in Brussels. Non-EU nationals can apply if based in an eligible country.

name: UKRI (UK Research and Innovation)
description: UKRI (UK Research and Innovation) is the umbrella body for nine UK research councils plus Innovate UK, the primary funder of business-led innovation. Innovate UK offers grants and loans to UK-based startups and SMEs across a wide range of programs: Smart Grants (open, technology-neutral, €25K–€500K); Knowledge Transfer Partnerships (KTPs, linking businesses with universities); and themed challenges aligned to clean growth, future mobility, AI, and healthy ageing. Applications go through the Innovate UK portal (UKRI Funding Service). Post-Brexit, UK entities are generally excluded from Horizon Europe but UKRI programs are open to UK-incorporated companies regardless of founder nationality.

name: GOBio Next (EIC / Horizon Europe)
amount: Up to €2.5M grant (proof of concept) + follow-on funding options
description: GO-Bio Next is a German federal program (BMBF) that funds life sciences spin-offs emerging from academic research. It runs in two phases: Phase 1 (Feasibility, up to ~€1.5M over 2 years) validates commercial viability and team formation, while Phase 2 (Company Formation, up to €2.5M) supports the actual founding and early growth of the biotech startup. Applicants must have a founding team rooted in a German research institution. The program is technology-neutral within life sciences, covering therapeutics, diagnostics, medical devices, and agricultural biotech.

name: EXIST Forschungstransfer
description: EXIST Forschungstransfer is the more intensive phase of the EXIST program, designed for spin-off projects that require substantial R&D to reach market readiness — typically deep tech with long development cycles. It runs in two phases: Phase 1 (up to 18 months, ~€180K+) funds R&D within the research institution; Phase 2 (up to 18 months) provides further support after company formation. Funding is significantly higher than the Gründerstipendium and requires a detailed technical and business plan. The host university applies on behalf of the team. Particularly suited to hardware, biotech, and materials science spin-offs.

name: Women TechEU
description: Women TechEU is an EIC initiative providing €75K business acceleration grants specifically to deep tech startups led by women CEOs. Beyond the grant, participants receive tailored coaching, mentoring from senior industry figures, and access to the broader EIC network and investor community. The program runs as an annual call and is designed to address the funding and visibility gap women founders face in European deep tech. Eligibility requires the startup to be in an early stage and the CEO to be a woman.

name: NEOTEC (CDTI)
description: NEOTEC is a CDTI (Centro para el Desarrollo Tecnológico Industrial) program for technology-based Spanish startups. It provides 0% interest loans (partially non-repayable) of up to €250K to companies less than 3 years old. Eligible startups must have a strong R&D component and a 3-year business plan. Unlike most grants, NEOTEC is a loan and must be partially repaid, though the repayment conditions are favorable. The program runs one or two calls per year. CDTI also offers follow-on instruments for more mature companies. Applicants must be incorporated in Spain.

name: Eurostars
amount: Up to €500K per project (national agency co-funding)
description: Eurostars is a joint program between EUREKA (38 member countries) and the European Commission that co-funds international R&D projects led by SMEs. Each project must involve at least two independent entities from different EUREKA countries, with an SME leading. National agencies fund their own country’s participants — meaning the actual grant is disbursed domestically, not centrally. Projects must have a clear commercial outcome within 2 years of completion. Eurostars has two annual cut-off dates and a fast evaluation process (~6 months from submission to funding decision).

name: EIC Transition
description: EIC Transition bridges the gap between early research results and market-ready products. It is exclusively open to teams and spin-offs that have completed an EIC Pathfinder or ERC Proof of Concept project. Funding of €500K–€2.5M supports technology maturation, prototype development, business model validation, and early IP strategy. Applicants can be research institutions, startups, or SMEs. The goal is to bring innovations from TRL 3–4 up to TRL 5–6, establishing a credible path to commercialization.

name: I-Nov Innovation Competition
description: I-Nov (Innovation Competition) is a French public innovation procurement program managed jointly by ADEME, ANR, and Bpifrance. It runs thematic calls across 12 priority areas including digital, health, transport and mobility, energy, and environment. Eligible applicants are French startups and SMEs with R&D projects of €1M–5M over 12–36 months. Co-financing covers 45–70% of eligible project costs depending on company size. I-Nov focuses on projects close to market with clear commercial potential, rather than fundamental research. Applications are submitted per thematic call.

name: aws Preseed & Seedfinancing
amount: Preseed: up to €89K–€100K; Seedfinancing: up to €356K–€400K (non-repayable grants)
description: aws Preseed & Seedfinancing is run by Austria Wirtschaftsservice (aws), the Austrian federal development and financing bank. It provides non-repayable grants to Austrian startups from idea stage through to market launch. Preseed (up to €100K) covers concept development, prototype building, and market validation. Seedfinancing (up to €400K) funds product development and early market entry. Both require an innovative product or service with a viable business model. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. aws also offers advisory services and connects funded startups with its broader investor and corporate network.

name: ERC Starting Grant
amount: Up to €1.5M over 5 years (up to €2.5M for relocating researchers)
description: The ERC Starting Grant is a European Research Council award for early-career researchers (2–7 years post-PhD) with an excellent research track record. It funds frontier, investigator-driven research in any scientific field at a European host institution. The PI must be employed by the host institution, which can be a university, research center, or private company with a research mission. ERC grants are not startup grants per se, but successful projects frequently generate IP and spin-off companies. The grant covers up to €1.5M over 5 years (up to €2.5M if the researcher relocates to Europe from abroad).

name: Innobooster (Innovation Fund Denmark)
amount: Up to DKK 5M (~€670K); 50–75% of eligible costs
description: Innobooster is Innovation Fund Denmark’s most accessible funding program for Danish startups and SMEs with innovative, knowledge-based projects. It offers two tracks: small projects (DKK 50K–2M, ~6-week processing time) and large projects (DKK 2M–5M, ~3-month processing time). It covers 50–75% of eligible costs. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. The program is broad in scope — any sector qualifies, with particular activity in greentech, life sciences, and digital. Innobooster is a good entry point to the Danish public funding ecosystem before moving to larger EU programs.

name: LIFE Programme
description: The LIFE Programme is the EU’s dedicated funding instrument for environment, nature, and climate action (2021–2027, total budget €5.4B). It operates through four sub-programs: Nature & Biodiversity, Circular Economy & Quality of Life, Climate Change Mitigation & Adaptation, and Clean Energy Transition. Projects are co-financed at 55–60% of eligible costs and typically involve a consortium of at least two entities. Project durations range from 2 to 5 years. CINEA (European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency) manages the program. Not primarily a startup grant — better suited to established companies or NGOs with a credible environmental track record.

name: Vinnova Innovation Fund
description: Vinnova is Sweden’s government innovation agency and manages a wide portfolio of funding programs for Swedish startups, SMEs, and research institutions. The primary startup-facing program is Innovative Startups, which provides SEK 500K–3M per project for companies under 5 years old with a genuinely new product or service. Thematic calls target sustainability, digitalization, health, and industrial transformation. Many Vinnova programs require a co-financing partner (e.g., a university or industry partner). Applications are submitted through Vinnova’s online portal and evaluated on innovation potential, team capability, and societal benefit.

name: EXIST Gründerstipendium
amount: €2,500–€3,000/month stipend per founder + €30K project budget (12 months)
description: EXIST-Gründerstipendium is a German federal program (BMWK) that supports knowledge-intensive, innovative startup ideas originating from universities and research institutions. It provides a monthly living stipend (€2,500 for graduates, €3,000 for post-docs, €2,000 for students) for up to 12 months, plus a €30K project budget for materials and coaching. Applicants must be affiliated with a German university, which acts as the host institution and applies on the team’s behalf. The program covers the idea and business plan validation phase only — the team is not yet expected to have a legal entity.

name: I-Lab Innovation Contest
description: I-Lab is an annual French innovation competition run since 1999 by Bpifrance and the Ministry of Higher Education & Research. It targets pre-startups and very early-stage startups building on scientific or technological breakthroughs. Two categories: ‘Emergence’ (for projects still in the research phase, grant up to €200K) and ‘Creation-Développement’ (for projects with a founding team and product in development, grant up to €600K). Winners also receive tailored support from Bpifrance and visibility at national innovation events. Applicants must be based in France.

name: EIT Accelerator (KIC Programs)
description: The EIT (European Institute of Innovation & Technology) funds Knowledge & Innovation Communities (KICs) — large-scale pan-European partnerships in specific sectors. Each KIC runs its own startup accelerator programs: EIT Climate-KIC (sustainability), EIT Digital (digital transformation), EIT Health (healthcare innovation), EIT Food (agri-food), EIT Manufacturing (industry), EIT Urban Mobility (transport), and EIT InnoEnergy (clean energy). Programs typically offer non-dilutive grants of €15K–€100K+, business plan competitions, education, mentoring, and access to a pan-European network. Applications go through the individual KIC, not centrally.

name: ESA BIC (Business Incubation Centres)
amount: €50K – €250K cash + in-kind support (varies by national BIC)
description: ESA Business Incubation Centres (BIC) are operated by the European Space Agency across 20+ sites in Europe (Austria, Belgium, Germany, Spain, Finland, France, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, UK, and others). Each national BIC provides cash grants (€50K–€250K depending on the country), access to ESA technology, expertise, and facilities, plus business support over a 2-year incubation period. Startups must be developing downstream satellite applications (e.g., Earth observation data services, navigation, telecommunications) or spin-ins that apply space technology to non-space markets. Applications go through the relevant national BIC.

name: SPRIND (Bundesagentur für Sprunginnovationen)
description: SPRIND (Bundesagentur für Sprunginnovationen) is Germany's federal agency for disruptive innovation, modeled on DARPA and ARPA-E. It identifies and funds 'radical innovations' that are too high-risk and long-horizon for incumbent companies or standard public funding. SPRIND runs themed challenge competitions where teams compete for milestone-based funding ranging from €100K to €10M+. Grants are non-repayable and outcome-driven. Crucially, SPRIND is nationality-agnostic — non-German and non-EU startups can and do receive funding, as long as they respond to a published challenge. SPRIND does not accept general applications; teams must respond to specific published challenges. It also has a Facilitation unit that helps innovators navigate legal and regulatory barriers.

name: FFG General Programme
amount: Up to €3M per project; 50% of costs (up to 70% for startups)
description: The FFG General Programme is the Austrian Research Promotion Agency’s (FFG) main open R&D funding instrument, available to Austrian companies of all sizes. It supports individual R&D projects (new products, processes, or services) and cooperative projects (with research institutions or other companies). Base subsidy rates are 25–35% for large companies, rising to 45–60% for SMEs and startups, and up to 70% for experimental development by small companies. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with a processing time of approximately 3 months. Thematic restrictions are minimal — the project must demonstrate clear innovation above the state of the art.

name: Cascade Funding
description: Cascade Funding (formally Financial Support to Third Parties, FSTP) is a mechanism through which EU-funded project hubs — such as AI testing and experimentation facilities, IoT platforms, and robotics hubs — redistribute a portion of their EU grant to third-party startups and SMEs via open competitive calls. Grant sizes are typically €5K–€200K. Each hub runs its own call with its own scope (tied to the hub’s technology focus), timeline, and eligibility criteria. Applications are submitted directly to the individual hub, not to the European Commission.
